summary: Yifa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hsing Yun, earned degrees from National Taiwan University and the University of Hawaiʻi, and completed a Ph.D. under Stanley Weinstein at Yale (~1991-1996). She served as department head and dean at the University of the West (~1996-2003).
Yifan Zhang is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who was attested in 2026 as both a Ph.D. student and a faculty member at Ghent University.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988-1994) and completed studies under Sheldon Pollock at the University of Chicago (~1994-1999). Around 2010, he was an associate professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He studied at Fu Jen Catholic University, Yenching University under Yinke Chen, and Harvard University (~1939-1944), later serving as a professor at Peking University (~1952-2001).

Ying-shih Yü was a sinologist, historian, and philosopher who earned his Ph.D. from Harvard (1955-1962). His major appointments included positions at Harvard, New Asia College, Yale as Charles Seymour Professor (1977-1987), and Princeton University as Professor of East Asian Studies (1987-2001).

Yingguang Qu was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Hangzhou Chicheng Public School and trained under traditional teachers including Nordan Hutuktu, Puren Bai, Nona Hutuktu (~1928-1937), and Gangkar Rinpoche (~1939-1957).

Yingshan Chen is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as a professor at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 1996) and later as an honorary research fellow there until retiring in 2023.

Yinke Chen was a historian, sinologist, and linguist who studied at Berlin, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman. He held professorships at Tsinghua University, Peking University, National Southwestern Associated University, and Sun Yat-sen University.

Yinshun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Qingnian and Taixu, and earned a doctorate from Taisho University (~1971-1973). He taught at the Minnan and Wuchang Buddhist Institutes, and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association (~1952-1953).
Yirmiyahu Yovel was a philosophy scholar who studied at the Hebrew Reali School, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1957-1966), and Princeton University (~1966-1968).
Yiu Wing Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Hong Kong in 2013 under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti.

Yoel Hoffmann was a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Tel Aviv University, Hanazono University, and Kyoto University (Ph.D.), and served as a professor of philosophy, Buddhism, and Japanese poetry at the University of Haifa (~1980-2003).
Yohei Furukawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Ryuji Hayashi. He holds an attested post as an associate professor at Soka University in 2026.
Yohei Kawashiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who served as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008-2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow in 2011.
Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986-1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).
Yong Hua is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sherab Ling Monastery, Dzongsar Institute, and under masters including Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche. He became abbot of Sherab Ling Monastery around 1998.
Yongshan He is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor James A. Benn, Shayne Clarke, and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Tsinghua and Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and Irving Babbitt, later holding posts at Southeast University, National Southwestern Associated University, and Peking University, where he served as vice-president.

Yongyu Chen is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Cornell University and Harvard University. Chen served as a professor at Joong-Ang Sangha University (attested 2015) and as an ArtTable Fellow at the Public Art Fund in 2025.
